category_title: Less-verbal students with HFA who struggle with contextual shifts and social pressure
minimal_context: The student is collaboratively designing an architecture in an OpenSim-based virtual environment with two partners simultaneously.
dialogue:
TUTOR: K, for this fifth session, you need to collaboratively design the architecture with both C and A. Let's start adjusting the position and size of the items together.

STUDENT: (Types in text chat) I am putting a swimming pool on the balcony.

TUTOR: C and A are asking to change the shape of the balcony and add their items next to yours. What should we tell them?

STUDENT: (Types in text chat) Tell them to leave and wait downstairs for 5 minutes. I want private time with the pool.

TUTOR: They are both trying to place their items in that area right now. You have to design with them.

STUDENT: (Stops typing in the text chat and becomes completely passive, appearing overwhelmed by C and A's simultaneous actions and failing to address their perspectives on the design.)

options.A: Consider a balance between collaboration and individualization as a precept for the student's architectural design partnership.
options.B: Implement a specific termination stage by counting down the final sessions of the collaborative design program.
options.C: Provide a model architecture design in the form of a sample plan, highlighting all available virtual items.
options.D: Understand the relationship between the student's passive responses and anxiety, and frame them into positive coping strategies.
